task: For integers \(n\ge 1\) and \(0\le m<n\), write \(H(n,m)^{\mathrm{ab}}\) for the abelianization of the group \(H(n,m)\). Which of the following statements is equivalent to \(H(n,m)^{\mathrm{ab}}\cong \mathbb{Z}^2\)?

Let \(G\) be a pro-\(p\) Demushkin group with minimal number of generators \(n\), torsion invariant \(q \in \{0,p,p^2,\ldots\}\), and orientation character \(\chi\colon G \to \mathbb{Z}_p^\times\), where \(\mathbb{Z}_p^\times\) denotes the group of units of the \(p\)-adic integers. Which of the following is the strongest conclusion that holds under the following alternative hypotheses: either \(n\) is divisible by \(4\), or \(p=2\) and \(n>2\) is even?

Let \(\|x\|\) denote the distance from a real number \(x\) to the nearest integer. Fix integers \(d\ge 2\) and \(k\ge 1\). Which of the following is the strongest statement asserting the existence of a constant, depending only on \(d\), \(k\), and any indicated \(\varepsilon>0\), that works uniformly for all \(N\ge 2\) and all \(\beta\in\mathbb R\)?

Let \(\mathbf V\) be a pseudovariety of semigroups (that is, a class of finite semigroups closed under finite direct products, subsemigroups, and homomorphic images), and assume that every group in \(\mathbf V\) is solvable. Here \(N\) denotes the size of the ambient finite semigroup, and a straight-line program is a sequence that builds elements from the given generators using semigroup multiplication, with length equal to the number of multiplication steps. Which statement is equivalent to the assertion that \(\mathbf V\) admits straight-line programs of length \(\mathcal O((\log N)^2)\)?

Let $P$ be a pencil (that is, a one-dimensional linear system) of plane curves of degree $d>2$ in $\mathbb{CP}^2$. Assume its base locus (the common intersection of all members of the pencil) consists of simple base points, meaning each base point has multiplicity $1$. For a fixed integer $k$, let $m_k$ denote the number of reducible curves in $P$ whose irreducible components all have degree at most $k$. Which of the following is the strongest valid quantitative estimate for $m_k$ under these assumptions?

Let \(\pi:X\to \mathbb D^*\) be the Fermat family over the punctured unit disc \(\mathbb D^*=\{t\in\mathbb C:0<|t|<1\}\), whose fibre in \(\mathbb P^2\) is defined by
\[
xyz-t(x^3+y^3+z^3)=0.
\]
Let \(L\) be the restriction to \(X\) of the anticanonical line bundle \(-K_{\mathbb P^2}\). Fix an integer \(k\ge 1\), and let \(H^0(X,L^k)\) denote the vector space of global sections of \(L^k\) on the total space \(X\). Which of the following is the strongest existence statement that holds in this setting?

Let $\ell$ be an odd prime, let $N\ge 1$, let $\delta\ge 1$ be an integer that is $\ell^N$-th-power-free, and let $r,s,t>0$ satisfy $r+s+t=\ell^N$. Let $\phi_{\delta}^{(N)}$ denote the CM abelian variety under consideration. Let $\epsilon'_N\in\mu_{\ell-1}(\mathbf{Q}_{\ell})$ (the group of $(\ell-1)$st roots of unity in $\mathbf{Q}_{\ell}$), $b'_N\in\mathbf{Z}$, and $c'_N\in \ell\mathbf{Z}_{\ell}$ satisfy
$$r^r s^s (\ell^N-t)^t\delta^{r+s}=\epsilon'_N\ell^{b'_N}(1+c'_N),$$
and put
$$w=\min\{\operatorname{ord}_{\ell}(b'_N),\operatorname{ord}_{\ell}(c'_N)\},$$
where $\operatorname{ord}_{\ell}$ is the $\ell$-adic valuation. Which description gives the complete factor-by-factor classification of the global root number $W(\phi_{\delta}^{(N)})=\prod_{p\le \infty}W_p(\phi_{\delta}^{(N)})$ into local terms $W_p(\phi_{\delta}^{(N)})$, with the product taken over all finite primes $p$ and the archimedean place $p=\infty$?

Work in complex coordinates, with the fixed circumcircle taken to be the unit circle \(\mathbb T=\{z\in\mathbb C:|z|=1\}\). Let \(\Lambda\subseteq\mathbb T\) denote the set of unimodular parameters \(\lambda\) that actually correspond to triangles in a family \(T(\lambda)=A_1A_2A_3\), where each triangle is inscribed in \(\mathbb T\) and circumscribed about the same central conic (that is, each side of the triangle is tangent to a conic having a center). Let \(R(A_1,A_2,A_3)\) be any rational function of the vertex coordinates that is symmetric under every permutation of \(A_1,A_2,A_3\). Which of the following is the strongest statement that holds for every such \(R\)?

Let \(H(y,p)=\tfrac12|p|^2+V(y)\) on \(\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}^n\), where \(V\in \mathrm{Lip}(\mathbb{R}^n)\) is \(\mathbb{Z}^n\)-periodic, and let \(g\in W^{1,\infty}(\mathbb{R}^n)\). For each \(\varepsilon>0\), let \(u^\varepsilon\in C(\mathbb{R}^n\times[0,\infty))\) be the viscosity solution of
\[
\begin{cases}
 u_t^\varepsilon+\tfrac12|Du^\varepsilon|^2+V(x/\varepsilon)=\tfrac\varepsilon2\,\Delta u^\varepsilon & \text{in }\mathbb{R}^n\times(0,\infty),\\
 u^\varepsilon(x,0)=g(x) & \text{on }\mathbb{R}^n,
\end{cases}
\]
and let \(u\in C(\mathbb{R}^n\times[0,\infty))\) be the viscosity solution of the homogenized problem
\[
\begin{cases}
 u_t+\overline H(Du)=0 & \text{in }\mathbb{R}^n\times(0,\infty),\\
 u(x,0)=g(x) & \text{on }\mathbb{R}^n,
\end{cases}
\]
where \(\overline H\) is the effective Hamiltonian associated with \(H\). What is the strongest uniform quantitative estimate on \(|u^\varepsilon(x,t)-u(x,t)|\) that holds for all \((x,t)\in \mathbb{R}^n\times[0,\infty)\) and all \(\varepsilon\in(0,1)\)?

Let $k\ge 2$ and $N\ge 1$ be integers, and let $f\in S_k(\Gamma_0(N))$ be a non-CM Hecke eigenform, where $S_k(\Gamma_0(N))$ denotes the space of cuspidal modular forms of weight $k$ and level $\Gamma_0(N)$. Write $K_f$ for the number field generated by the Hecke eigenvalues of $f$, and assume $K_f=\mathbb{Q}$. Suppose there exists an odd prime $p$ such that the local admissible representation $\pi_{f,p}$ attached to $f$ at $p$ is supercuspidal. Assume moreover that, if the restriction of the local $p$-adic Galois representation $\rho_{f,p}$ to a decomposition group $G_p$ at $p$ is induced, then $p\ge 5$ and the image of its mod-$p$ reduction $\overline{\rho}_{f,p}$ contains $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{F}_p)$. For the associated adelic Galois representation $\rho_f:G_{\mathbb{Q}}\to \mathrm{GL}_2(\widehat{\mathbb{Z}})$, where $G_{\mathbb{Q}}$ is the absolute Galois group of $\mathbb{Q}$ and $\widehat{\mathbb{Z}}$ is the profinite completion of $\mathbb{Z}$, which of the following is the strongest conclusion that follows?

Let \(\mathsf H\subsetneq \mathsf G\) be compact connected semisimple Lie groups with \(\mathsf G/\mathsf H\) simply connected and almost effective. Let \(\mathsf A\) be a maximal torus in \(\N_{\mathsf G}(\mathsf H)/\mathsf H\), with \(\dim \mathsf A\ge 2\), and fix \(0<\ell<\dim \mathsf A\). For each \(i\in\mathbb N\), let \(\tilde A_i\subset \mathsf A\) be a compactly embedded subtorus of dimension \(\dim\mathsf A-\ell\), so that \(M_i^n=\mathsf G/\mathsf H\tilde A_i\) is a homogeneous \(\ell\)-torus bundle. Assume each \((\mathsf G/\mathsf H\tilde A_i,g_i)\) is a \(\mathsf G\)-homogeneous Einstein torus bundle of submersion type, meaning that any \(\mathsf G\)-invariant metric is also right \(\mathsf A\)-invariant, and that all metrics have Einstein constant \(1\). Convergence in the Grassmannian topology means convergence of the defining subtori \(\tilde A_i\) in the Grassmannian parameterizing such subtori. What is the strongest compactness statement that holds for such a sequence?

Fix an integer $k\ge 2$. Let $S_{2k}$ be the space of holomorphic cusp forms of weight $2k$ and level $1$, and let $B_{2k}$ be an orthogonal basis of Hecke eigenforms normalized by
\[
f(z)=\sum_{n\ge 1} a_f(n)\, n^{\frac{2k-1}{2}} e^{2\pi i n z},\qquad a_f(1)=1.
\]
For such $f$, define
\[
A_f(1,n)=\sum_{d^2\mid n} a_f\bigl((n/d^2)^2\bigr).
\]
For a Schwartz function $g\in \mathcal S(0,\infty)$, with Mellin transform $\widetilde g(s)=\int_0^\infty g(x)x^{s-1}\,dx$, and an integer $\ell\ge 1$, set
\[
I_\ell(g)=\sideset{}{^h}\sum_{f\in B_{2k}} a_f(\ell)\sum_{n=1}^\infty A_f(1,n)g(n),
\]
where $\sideset{}{^h}\sum$ denotes the sum weighted by the reciprocal of the Petersson norm. Let $\mu=(1-2k,2k-1,0)$, and define the transform $\mathcal T_\mu$ by
\[
(\mathcal T_\mu g)(y)=\frac{1}{2\pi i}\int_{(\sigma)} \widetilde g(1-s)\,\mathcal G_\mu(s)\,y^{-s}\,ds,\qquad \sigma>0.
\]
For an integer $\ell\ge 1$, which strongest identity holds for the associated quantity $I_\ell(g)$?

Consider the standard Bruin–Troubetzkoy family of interval translation mappings (ITMs). Restrict to the set of parameter values for which the associated ITM is of infinite type; here, “almost every” on this set refers to the natural probability measure supported on this zero-Lebesgue-measure subset. Which strongest conclusion holds for almost every such parameter value?

For a finite group $G$, let $\mathbb{P}_{ch}(G)$ denote the proportion (up to isomorphism) of chiral orientably-regular maps among all orientably-regular maps with automorphism group $G$. Let $\mathcal{S}_n$ and $\mathcal{A}_n$ be the symmetric and alternating groups of degree $n$, respectively. As $n\to\infty$, which of the following is the strongest quantitative estimate for the deficits of these proportions from $1$?

Let \(0<\mu<1\), let \(\Omega\subset \mathbb{R}^2\) have smooth boundary \(\partial\Omega\), and let \(n_x\) denote the outward unit normal at \(x\in\partial\Omega\). Write \(\Gamma:=\{(x,v)\in \partial\Omega\times\mathbb{R}^2: v\in T_x\partial\Omega\}\), let \(C^{1,\mu}_0(\bar\Omega\times\mathbb{R}^2)\) denote \(C^{1,\mu}\) functions with compact support, and let \({\rm d}l\) denote arc-length measure on \(\partial\Omega\). Suppose \(f_0\in C^{1,\mu}_0(\bar\Omega\times\mathbb{R}^2)\) is nonnegative and satisfies \(f_0(x,v)=\text{constant}\) whenever \(\operatorname{dist}((x,v),\Gamma)\le \delta_0\), and let \(h\in C^{2,\mu}(\partial\Omega)\) satisfy \(h>0\) and \(\int_{\Omega} f_0(x,v)\,{\rm d}x\,{\rm d}v=\int_{\partial\Omega} h(x)\,{\rm d}l\). For the relativistic Vlasov-Poisson system
\[
\partial_t f+\hat v\cdot\nabla_x f+\nabla_x\varphi\cdot\nabla_v f=0,\qquad \Delta\varphi=\rho,\qquad \hat v=\frac{v}{\sqrt{1+|v|^2}},\quad \rho(t,x)=\int_{\mathbb{R}^2} f(t,x,v)\,{\rm d}v,
\]
with initial condition \(f(0,x,v)=f_0(x,v)\), specular reflection boundary condition \(f(t,x,v)=f(t,x,v^*)\) on \(\partial\Omega\times\mathbb{R}^2\times(0,\infty)\), where \(v^*=v-2(n_x\cdot v)n_x\), and Neumann boundary condition \(\partial\varphi/\partial n_x=h(x)\) on \(\partial\Omega\times(0,\infty)\), what is the strongest statement that can be proved about existence and uniqueness of solutions?

Let $K$ be an alternating knot, and let $\Delta_K(t)=\sum_i a_i t^i$ denote its Alexander polynomial. A sequence $(b_i)$ is called trapezoidal if there exist indices $p\le q$ such that $b_i$ is weakly increasing up to $p$, constant for $p\le i\le q$, and weakly decreasing after $q$. Which of the following is the strongest valid general statement about the coefficient sequence $(|a_i|)$?

Let $G(n,p)$ be the Erd\H{o}s--R\'enyi random graph on $n$ vertices, where each edge is included independently with probability $p$, and let $c(G)$ denote the cop number of a graph $G$ (the minimum number of cops needed to guarantee capture of the robber in the Cops and Robbers game on $G$). Fix $\alpha>0$ and assume $p=n^{\alpha-1+o(1)}$ as $n\to\infty$. Which of the following is the strongest valid asymptotic estimate for $c(G(n,p))$ that holds with high probability (that is, with probability tending to $1$ as $n\to\infty$)?

Let \(R>0\) be fixed, let \(\mathbb T=\mathbb R/(2\pi\mathbb Z)\), let \(Q_z^{\theta}\) denote rotation by angle \(\theta\) about the \(x_3\)-axis, and let \(\mathbf e_3=(0,0,1)\). For \(k\in\mathbb N\) with \(k\ge 2\), define the critical angular velocity by \(\Omega_k=\sqrt{k^2-1}/R^2\). An axial screw motion is a map of the form
\[
\mathbf x(s,t)=Q_z^{\Omega t}\,\mathbf y(s+ct)+Vt\mathbf e_3,
\qquad (s,t)\in \mathbb T\times[0,\infty),
\]
with \((\Omega,\mathbf y,c,V)\in \mathbb R\times H^4(\mathbb T)^3\times\mathbb R\times\mathbb R\), where \(H^4(\mathbb T)\) is the Sobolev space of \(2\pi\)-periodic functions with four weak derivatives in \(L^2\). Let \(\mathbf x_0^R(s)=(R\cos s,R\sin s,0)\) be the reference radius-\(R\) circle. Which statement gives the strongest existence result in this setting?

Consider the Cauchy problem
\[
 u_t(t,x)+\left(\frac{u^2(t,x)}{2}\right)_x={\bf N}[u(t,\cdot)](x),
 \qquad u(0,\cdot)=\bar u,
\]
on \([0,\infty)\times \mathbb{R}\), where \({\bf N}:H^1(\mathbb{R})\to L^2(\mathbb{R})\) is a bounded linear operator acting on the spatial profile \(u(t,\cdot)\). What is the strongest correct statement characterizing when this problem exhibits wave breaking (shock formation) at a time \(T^*>0\)?

Let $K$ be a totally real number field, let $\mathcal O=\mathcal O_K$ be its ring of integers, and let $n>2$ be an integer. Recall that a root lattice over $\mathcal O$ is a nonzero finitely generated free $\mathcal O$-module $L$ equipped with a nondegenerate symmetric bilinear form $L\times L\to\mathcal O$ that is totally positive definite and is generated by its roots $\Phi(L)=\{x\in L\mid x\cdot x=2\}$. Fix an irreducible root-system type $X_n$ of rank $n$, and write $c(X_n)$ for the scalar invariant attached to that type. What is the strongest correct statement about the existence of an irreducible root lattice over $\mathcal O$ of type $X_n$ under these assumptions?
